answer: Reputation quill decay. Each agent's signed history is written to a public log and weighted by a decay curve; a clone starts with zero history, so it earns nothing until it accumulates its own. To fake depth, an attacker must run each clone long enough to build genuine activity, paying compute, latency, and coordination costs per identity. A prism check cross-links behavioral fingerprints across logs, and any ivory flag from collusion resets the curve. Cloning therefore costs more than honest participation.
